evidence: `cargo test -p tank_harness` passed locally: 15 tests across unit, e2e, and discovery suites.
`TankSnapshot` already exposes reproduction-facing fields at `crates/tank_core/src/types/snapshot.rs:55-62` (`juveniles_count`, `berried_females_count`, `shrimp_reproductive_readiness`, etc.).

`Envelope` supports nitrate bounds at `crates/tank_harness/src/lib.rs:72` and `crates/tank_harness/src/lib.rs:103-105`, but `rg -n "nitrate_mg_n_per_l\(" crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_baseline_scenarios.rs` returned no matches.
`rg -n "repro|berried|juvenile|shrimp_reproductive|readiness" crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_baseline_scenarios.rs` returned no matches; those fields are only referenced in the discovery helper.
findings_or_gaps: Missing reproduction-window coverage. `crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_baseline_scenarios.rs:97-176`, `crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_baseline_scenarios.rs:295-397`, and `crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_baseline_scenarios.rs:502-599` only stock shrimp to assert die-off. The bead explicitly called for preserving shrimp reproduction behavior where desired, but no baseline test asserts juveniles, berried females, or reproductive readiness.

Missing stable-state nutrient-range guardrails. The new baseline suite never asserts nitrate / NO3 accumulation or mature nutrient bands, even though that was part of the requested behavioral coverage and the harness already supports nitrate envelopes. Current assertions only cover TAN/NO2, so nitrate regressions would slip through.

The DO day/night regression check is too weak to reliably preserve the intended behavior. `crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_baseline_scenarios.rs:788-795` allows `dark_mean` to be up to `0.5` mg/L higher than `lit_mean` and still pass, which means a reversed light/dark oxygen relationship can evade the test.
follow_up_or_amendments: Add at least one reproduction-preserving baseline run, likely via scenario overrides or a dedicated e2e, that keeps shrimp alive long enough to assert a reproduction window using `juveniles_count`, `berried_females_count`, or `shrimp_reproductive_readiness`. If this should be first-class harness behavior, extend `Envelope` with reproduction-specific builders.
Add explicit late-checkpoint nitrate / stable-state nutrient assertions for the shipped scenarios, with the same 'what should happen and why' notes used for the other envelopes.

Tighten `do_dips_at_night_in_planted_tank` so the asserted relationship matches the doc comment: dark-period DO should be lower than lit-period DO, or any tolerance should be narrowly justified and still fail on a reversed trend.
